The *Nāgapallavattheraapadāna* is a biographical poem preserved in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Tipiṭaka (catalogued as Tha-Ap 417) [SuttaCentral]. Like other texts in the Apadāna, it recounts the past-life devotional deeds and karmic fruits associated with a Buddhist elder [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of this work across five languages [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallels or cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are recorded [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis identifies 62 matching passages shared with 28 other Pali texts, highlighting the highly formulaic character of Apadāna verse compositions [DharmaNexus]. The text shares extensive verse runs—particularly between segments §2.2 and §8.1—with other poems in the collection, such as the *Ketakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 516), the *Nāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 517), the *Pāṭihīrasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 435), and the *Saḷalamaṇḍapiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 400) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, lines from segment §3 (§3.1–3.4) are paralleled in the first volume of the Theragāthā commentary (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus].
